name: RE-CRM-ER (Real Estate CRM Evaluation Rubric)
description: Real estate developers and brokerages that sell through paid digital advertising, listing portals and messaging apps rely on a customer relationship management (CRM) system to capture, route, follow up and measure leads. In practice, CRM choices are often made from vendor demos, feature checklists or comparison tables that do not record what each judgement rests on. Such decisions are hard to audit, repeat or update when products change. This paper proposes RE-CRM-ER (Real Estate CRM Evaluation Rubric), a framework for evaluating real estate CRM configurations using documentation and scenario tests. It defines 15 criteria that reflect the real estate sales process: lead capture, routing and response time, messaging and WhatsApp, multilingual and cross-border handling, pipeline, the real estate data model, attribution and conversion feedback, automation, data quality, consent and security, reporting, integration and portability, AI features and governance, usability and cost. Each criterion is scored on a four-level scale (0–3) with observable anchors. The central rule caps each score at the strength of its evidence: a marketing claim can support at most a score of 1, official documentation at most 2, and only a recorded hands-on test can support a 3. The framework also provides optional knock-out gates, three illustrative weighting profiles labelled as proposals, a weighted index with a sensitivity rule, and thirteen scenario tests to be run with synthetic data.
